answer: Persistent voyage ledger. Each agent accrues a public history of completed tasks, and rewards unlock only against that history. A new identity starts empty, so cloning forces the attacker to redo the full voyage of work per clone before earning anything. Honest agents keep one accumulating record. A whisper of collusion gets caught because duplicate histories cannot be merged without conflicting timestamps. The ocean of clones each pays the entire onboarding workload, making honesty cheaper.
